findings.title: Distributed witness fields
findings.claim: The imperative turns the brothers' truth claim into a request for corroboration from more than one public body: a settled community and a traveling caravan.
findings.mechanism: The focus asking form addresses an external source of information, while the settlement and caravan are collective carriers; wider verification and settlement-route relations make the request function as public checking rather than private assertion.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see credibility moving outward into a network of witnesses, with the town and caravan functioning as distinct social locations for checking the report.
findings.containment: The relation does not make every inhabitant or caravan member an infallible witness, and it does not decide whether the brothers' entire account is correct.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers and cited connection targets are exact, but the reader-walk support is legacy-unbound and the connection rows supply relation notes without full target morphology; the finding is therefore retained with explicit qualification.

findings.title: A truth claim scoped to witnessed report
findings.claim: The emphatic claim of truth can describe a sincere report of what was witnessed even while the scene's apparent interpretation remains false.
findings.mechanism: The retrospective 12:90 distinction narrows the claim to witnessed reporting, while the supplied 12:51 relation joins truthful speech to both a question and an acknowledged limit of knowledge; the focus predicate therefore carries a scoped testimony rather than an exhaustive account of every hidden fact.
findings.reader_payoff: Truth and the total situation can remain distinct without cancelling one another: a report may be sincere and locally accurate while an apparent theft is not the whole truth of the scene.
findings.containment: This preserves the ordinary claim that the speakers call themselves truthful; it does not pronounce the entire event innocent, settle every unseen fact, or rank sincerity over objective truth. The supplied 27:49 row also preserves a contrary setting in which claims of truth and lack of witnesses occur within a false scheme.

epistemic.reason: The reader-walk supplies the explicit 12:90 before-and-after distinction and the focus carrier is exact, but the source is legacy-unbound and the wider rows are authored relations rather than complete target analyses.

findings.title: The place-name as a public body
findings.claim: The settlement named in the imperative can stand for its inhabitants, so asking the town addresses a gathered community as a witness body.
findings.mechanism: The settlement branch explicitly permits a place-name to denote its people, and the wider settlement-route relation supplies a concrete social setting; the place-name therefore compresses the public body into the location named by the sentence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears a public audit rather than an impossible request addressed to buildings: the brothers direct their father toward a community that can remember and report.
findings.containment: This is a bounded metonymy. It does not claim that every inhabitant saw the event, that the community speaks with one voice, or that public corroboration automatically resolves the father's doubt.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch, focus occurrence, and reader-walk support are exact, while the support is legacy-unbound and the wider connection supplies only a qualified relation note.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus carrier and target Arabic are supplied, while the connection rows are discovery nominations without trust labels or full target morphology; the finding remains exploratory and bounded to testability.
